config.description: Distilled student on dozken's architecture at v022's exact size (hidden 160, 321,602 params), but trained with batch_sequences 64 instead of 16 -- the batch size his own notes cite. Same teacher, same model, same loss; the training regime is the only change.
config.hypothesis: The 0.0116 between v021 (his architecture, our recipe, 0.678575) and his own model (same architecture, 0.690168) is in his TRAINING, not his network. His notes cite batch 64, chunk 1000, 5 epochs; we use chunk 1000 but batch 16. A 4x larger batch changes the gradient noise scale, and for a tail-weighted global Pearson objective that plausibly matters a lot. If the missing 0.0116 is anywhere we can reach, it is here. v023 and v024 are independent: one tests the student size, this one tests the regime.
config.change_vs_parent: batch_sequences 16 -> 64 only. Same hidden 160, same teacher, same loss, same 3 epochs. Total samples and total compute are unchanged; only the batch geometry differs. Steps per epoch fall 4x (13,259 -> 3,315) because a step consumes one chunk per lane.

train_time_metrics.aggregation: mean of two target-wise global clipped Weighted Pearson correlations over all masked rows

score_interpretation: full_valid_wp 0.684818, trained on cache/train alone, clean. -0.000410 against v022's 0.685228 = -1.3 sigma, inside the noise floor. Batch 64 does NOT recover the 0.0116 that separates our reproduction of his architecture (v021, 0.678575) from his own weights (0.690168), so the training-regime hypothesis is refuted at least in batch size. Worth recording HOW: v024 led v022 by +0.0092 at step 2,499 and +0.0068 at step 4,999, reaching 99.9% of v022's FINAL score by step 4,999, then converged 0.0004 BELOW it. Judged mid-training that reads as a large win. AGENTS.md 11.3 warns against exactly this and the warning is correct. The real result is speed: 2.39h vs 5.31h, 2.2x less compute for the same score, which is what makes a 5-epoch recipe affordable. Not a promotion candidate: v022 remains our best.
promotion_verdict: Not a promotion candidate. v022 remains the best model at 0.685228 local / 0.6565 public. This run is packaged and documented as a refuted result on the axis it tested.
latency_verdict: Passes the retired-then-replaced latency gate. Note the grader has now returned actual times for v021 (55m32s, 93%) and v022 (50m46s, 85%), both of which our old 75% margin wrongly rejected, so a projection in the 85% band is known to complete.
